title: Drawing diagrams by just asking ChatGPT

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A teammate describes a flow in chat, and ten minutes later you need a sequence diagram in your repo. What's the fastest way to get there?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Honestly? A photo of the whiteboard and a lot of squinting.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ha, that was Antoine's problem too. A whiteboard photo doesn't paste into a Markdown repo, and typing PlantUML from memory is slow. So he built D2C OpenAI Plugin, a ChatGPT plugin that turns a conversation into a real diagram without leaving the thread.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What kind of diagrams are we talking about?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three formats. PlantUML for UML sequences, classes and deployments. Mermaid for diagrams that GitHub shows natively. And D2 for modern, declarative system sketches. The point is text-native diagrams he can drop into blog posts, READMEs and design reviews.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So how does it work in practice?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You name the diagram type in your request. The model writes the syntax, the plugin sends it to the right renderer, and you paste the result into your Markdown. Think of the plugin as a switchboard operator: it connects your request to the right drawing tool.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A good one from the post: a PlantUML sequence with a user, a React app, FastAPI and Postgres, including the login and a cache miss path. Another asks for a Mermaid flowchart of a CI pipeline, from git push through lint, test, build image and deploy on AWS. And a D2 diagram of a homelab with Caddy on EC2, CloudWatch logs and Lambda alerts.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's quite a range from one chat box.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It is, and it fits the same habit as his later work with AIPRM prompt templates, just wired in as a plugin action. The post has a screenshot and an animated demo of diagrams appearing right in the ChatGPT thread.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Has the idea moved on since the plugin era?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Antoine carried the same loop forward with uml-mcp, which brings diagram generation to Cursor and other M C P hosts. Same idea, new home.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the takeaway is that diagrams can be a conversation.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. Say what you want drawn, get text you can version and share. The full write-up has the demo and the example prompts if you want to try them.
